quotes.text: Azure Key Vault is a cloud-based digital safe for your secrets. It's a managed service from Microsoft for storing API keys, database passwords, connection strings, encryption keys, and certificates in one central place.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear plain-English definition of Azure Key Vault and what it stores.

quotes.text: Most people look at the key vault contributor role and think it's safe. They see the word contributor and assume they can manage the vault settings, but not touch the secrets inside.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the most common and dangerous permission misconception around Key Vault.

quotes.text: This is the closest thing to credentialless authentication in Azure. It's a game changer for security because it eliminates the most common attack vector, stolen credentials. If there are no credentials to steal, there's nothing for an attacker to compromise.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why managed identity fundamentally improves security.

quotes.text: Identity is the perimeter, not the network. It doesn't matter if someone is inside your virtual network or outside it. What matters is whether they have a valid identity with the right permissions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the identity-first security principle in a memorable way.

quotes.text: Key vault is your digital safe, but it's only as secure as the access controls you put around it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's core message into one sentence.

chapters.title: Secrets in code are a risk
How it all connects and what to do now

takeaways: Azure Key Vault centralizes secrets, keys and certificates so credentials never live in code or config files and can be rotated in one place.
Switch from legacy access policies to Azure RBAC and audit the Key Vault Contributor role, because with legacy policies a contributor can grant itself access to every secret.
Use managed identities, separate vaults per environment, and enable soft delete and purge protection to build a secure, low-cost secret management foundation.
hook: API keys and database passwords hard-coded in config files are one push away from being exposed. This episode explains Azure Key Vault in plain English for developers and cloud admins: what to store in it, how access control really works, the contributor-role trap that exposes secrets, and why managed identity is the gold standard.
